title: Trace search results with equal timestamp_ms have no defined order; tests must not assert by position
answers: trace search returns traces in wrong order intermittently
traces created in same millisecond come back in random order from search
how do I write a test that checks traces returned by search
body:
Symptom: Trace search tests fail intermittently with a wrong count or wrong assessments on a trace (e.g. `assert 1 == 3`), even though the search results are correct; the failure depends on timing.
Root cause: tests/tracing/test_assessment.py:test_search_traces_with_assessments indexed results by position (traces[0], traces[1]) and assumed creation order. Search orders by timestamp_ms ascending, and traces created in the same millisecond are tie-broken on the random request_id, so position is not creation order.
Fix pattern: Build a dict keyed by trace_id from the returned traces (`{t.info.trace_id: t for t in traces}`) and look up each expected trace by the id of the span it was created from, then assert on that trace.
Constraints: Applies to tests that create several traces quickly and then check search output. If a test needs a specific order, it must order by a key that is unique per trace (not timestamp_ms alone). The fix is test-only; do not change the store's tie-break to make tests pass.
applies: Tests in tests/tracing/ that assert on the results of trace search with order_by=timestamp_ms or similar time-based ordering.
says: Trace search returns simultaneously created traces in an unpredictable order instead of creation sequence.
Traces logged at the exact same millisecond appear in random order in search results.
Trace assessment test suite intermittently fails when checking evaluation results across search.
Evaluation assessment checks on trace search fail randomly when multiple traces share timestamps.
search: Trace search results ordered by timestamp_ms have no defined tie-break order for traces created in the same millisecond, so tests must not assert by position. In tests/tracing/test_assessment.py:test_search_traces_with_assessments, tests should construct a dictionary keyed by trace_id from search results rather than indexing by position. Applies to tests in tests/tracing/ asserting on time-ordered trace search results, which must order by a unique key if a specific sequence is required. This fix is strictly test-only and the underlying store tie-break behavior must not be changed.
